context: Linked force-directed network + scrollable table showing community detection results: 100 nodes, 404 edges, 5 communities, with bidirectional highlight on node/community click
first_impression: Immediately readable — five well-separated clusters with convex hull outlines and a clean 5-color Tol Bright palette that carries consistently into the table.
what_works: Community structure is unambiguous at a glance: hulls, color, and spatial separation all reinforce the same grouping; the 5-color palette is perceptually distinct and colorblind-safe, and its consistent use across both views eliminates any legend-matching effort. Table grouping by community with inline betweenness bars and sticky headers keeps tabular detail well-organized.
what_doesnt: The table lists all 100 nodes sequentially, so comparing metrics across communities requires scrolling rather than simultaneous inspection — clicking a community header auto-scrolls but you can only see one group at a time; animation/interaction fidelity (node drag reheating the simulation, transition staging) cannot be assessed from the static screenshot.
